questions.question: The father of a girl is three years older than her mother. Six years ago, the average age of the girl and her parents was 32 years, and the age of the father was twice the present age of his daughter. What is the present age (in years) of the mother?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The Father of a girl is three years older than his mother.

The average age of the girl and her parents six years ago was 32 years and the age of the father was twice the present age of the girl.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average of observations × number of observations

**Calculation:**

Let the present age of the girl is 'x' 

So, the age of the father six years ago was '2x'

The age of the girl six years ago was 'x - 6'

The father of a girl is three years older than his mother. So, the mother's age was '2x - 3'

The total age of the girl and her parents six years ago was 32 × 3 = 96 years

The total age of the girl and her parents six years ago was 2x + 2x - 3 + x - 6 = 96 years

5x = 96 + 9 

5x = 105 

x = 21

The age of mother six years ago was 2x - 3 = 2 × 21 - 3 = 39 years

The present age of mother will be 39 + 6 = 45 years

questions.question: If a shopkeeper purchases a certain number of items for a certain sum and sells a fraction of the said number for the same amount, then his profit is 300%. What is the fraction?
questions.solution:
Given:

The shopkeeper purchases a certain number of items for a certain sum and sells a fraction of the said number for the same amount, then his profit is 300%

Concept used: 

Profit% = {(Selling Price - Cost Price) over Cost Price} times 100\%

Calculation:

Let's suppose the shopkeeper purchases P unit of an item at Rs. Q and sells R unit of at Rs. Q.

Hence, the cost price of each unit item = Rs. (Q/P)

Hence, the selling price of each unit item = Rs. (Q/R)

Profit = {Q over R} - {Q over P}

According to the question,

{Q over R} - {Q over P} over {Q over P} × 100 = 300

⇒ (P - R) over R = 3

⇒ {P over R} - 1 = 3

⇒ {P over R} = 4

⇒ {R over P} = {1 over 4}

**∴ The fraction is {1 over 4}.**

questions.question: What is the full form of OCD?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Obsessive-Compulsive Device.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **The full form of OCD is Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.**
 
• Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a **mental and behavioural disorder **in which an individual has intrusive thoughts and feels the need to perform certain routines repeatedly to the extent where it induces distress or impairs general function.
 
• As indicated by the disorder's name, the primary symptoms of OCD are obsessions and compulsions.
 
• Obsessions are persistent unwanted thoughts,** mental images, or urges that generate feelings of anxiety, disgust, or discomfort.**
 
• Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is characterized by the occurrence of unwanted, intrusive obsessive thoughts and distressing images which are usually accompanied by compulsive behaviours. Compulsive behaviours are carried out either to undo or neutralize the obsessions or to prevent the occurrence of some dreadful event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anxiety disorders **are disorders that decrease the performance or social functioning of an individual due to hyper-anxiety.

 
 
• Anxiety disorder can be of many types such as generalized anxiety disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, somatoform disorder, etc.
 
 
 
• **Obsessive behaviour** is the inability to stop thinking about a particular idea or topic.
 
 
• The person involved, often finds these thoughts to be unpleasant and shameful.
 
 
 
• **Compulsive behaviour** is the need to perform certain behaviours over and over again.
 
 
• Many compulsions deal with counting, ordering, checking, touching, and washing.
 
• People affected by the obsessive-compulsive disorder are unable to control their preoccupation with specific ideas or are unable to prevent themselves from repeatedly carrying out a particular act or series of acts that affect their ability to carry out normal activities.
